name: module-size-inventory
body: Branch-graph inventory of decomposition SIGNALS — prompts to inspect a module, not targets. 32 first-party files exceed the ~400-line signal (excluding `vendor/` and `.md`): 22 exceed 1000, 12 exceed 2000. The longest root-crate files are `src/main.rs` (10,403 lines; production ends around line 2811), `src/plan_cmd.rs` (7,469; ~2,156 production), `src/layers.rs` (5,720), `src/splice.rs` (4,317), `src/ingest.rs` (4,000), `src/load.rs` (3,505), `src/project_cmd.rs` (2,986; ~628 production), `src/artifacts.rs` (2,300), `src/node_cmd.rs` (2,137), `src/cache.rs` (2,022). The dominant cause is inline `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`: ~675 test functions (142 unit, 8 int, 310 e2e) across 23 files; `src/main.rs`'s tests span lines 2822–10401 (~73% of the file), and `src/node_cmd.rs` is ~438 production vs 1,697 test. The frontend crates carry the same kind of signal: `src/structlib/src/main.rs` (2,617), `src/javalib/CallGraphBuilder.java` (2,034), `src/pylib/src/main.rs` (1,968), `src/cpplib/main.cpp` (1,745), `src/rustlib/src/main.rs` (1,715), `src/golib/main.go` (1,390), `src/csharplib/Program.cs` (1,201), `src/tslib/scanner.ts` (1,053). Each is a prompt to inspect cohesion — never a mandate to split. [with user] The law now applies repo-wide (root crate + eight frontend crates), so this inventory is the signal set the decomposition review starts from.
